Map of Nigeria showing the locations of the early centres of civilization. Points marked and labelled: "Iwo Eleru" (south-west, near Akure), "Ife" (south-west), "Benin" (mid-west), "Igbo-Ukwu" (south-east, near Awka), "Nok" (central, north of the Niger-Benue confluence, covering parts of Kaduna/Plateau), and "Daima" (far north-east, south of Lake Chad).

An illustration of the famous Igbo-Ukwu roped bronze pot. A rounded bronze vessel sitting on a small stand, completely enclosed in a delicate, decorative net of bronze ropes tied in knots, cast as a single piece. The metal has a greenish-brown patina.

A cross-section diagram of a traditional defensive moat and wall (like the Benin Iya). On the left, a deep, steep-sided V-shaped ditch (moat). The earth dug from the ditch is piled high on the right side to form a massive, steep earthen wall (bank). A tiny human figure stands at the bottom of the ditch to show the massive scale.
